title: Robust Stage Design for Monotone Rollouts with Common-Uniform Threshold Assignment
banked_reason: D0.5 exhausted three carried revise rounds: the exact covariance reduction, attained min-sup, and fixed-parameter small-budget exponent are sound, but field lift requires the unresolved global node-weight optimizer, matching leading constant, active-block dual certificate, and Chebyshev-Lobatto regime map.
gap_reasons: The exact covariance reduction/attained min-sup and fixed-parameter q exponent are valid but field lift requires the exact global node-weight optimizer, matching leading constant, active-block dual certificate, and Chebyshev-Lobatto win/loss/tie regimes.
The required lift is exactly the declared oeq:analytic-node-weight-frontier, a genuine open problem rather than a bounded D0 repair.
proof_attempt_summary: D0 verified the exact common-uniform covariance identity, reduced the robust design problem to an attained spectral min-sup over the declared aggregate-coefficient ellipsoid, and proved finite-sample radius coverage plus the fixed-parameter small-budget exponent. Three carried D0.5 revisions exhausted all bounded improvements while math review remained clean. The field-tier lift would require solving the genuinely open global node-weight optimizer, exact leading constant, active-block dual certificate, and Chebyshev-Lobatto regime map, so the sound result is banked at subfield tier.
tldr: A monotone production ramp assigns unit \(i\) at every fraction by the same threshold rule \(Z_i(u)=\mathbf 1\{U_i\le u\}\). Over the declared permutation-invariant ellipsoid for aggregate coefficients of a \(\beta\)-order finite-population schedule, the exact cross-stage covariance is a subset-intersection kernel rather than the diagonal or total-variation envelope used in existing rollout bounds. The kernel reduces the exponentially large robust eigenvalue to \(\beta+1\) subset-lattice isotypic blocks and turns joint node-and-weight choice into an attained exact spectral minimum. A leading eigenvector gives an explicit legal finite-valued least-favourable schedule for every fixed design, while a uniform-node Lagrange readout and the degree-moment barrier prove the sharp fixed-parameter small-budget law \(V^*_{n,\beta,k,q,\delta(q)}=\Theta(q^{1-2\beta})\), uniformly over admissible spacing rules. The same design-computable radius certificate yields a finite-sample Chebyshev confidence interval without a central limit theorem or an outcome-estimated variance. An analytic global optimizer, the exact leading constant, and the Chebyshev--Lobatto regime map remain open.
gap: Cortez, Eichhorn, and Yu derive polynomial-interpolation estimators for nested Bernoulli rollouts and control their variance by spacing bounds, while the accepted Chebyshev-envelope result optimizes a positive-semidefinite diagonal envelope. Neither result characterizes the covariance matrices attainable when every stage thresholds the same unit uniforms, and neither supplies a least-favourable legal schedule for that covariance.
fill: The project identifies the exact monomial covariance kernel, exploits permutation symmetry to reduce the robust covariance operator to small subset-lattice blocks, formulates the joint rollout-node and polynomial-exact-weight infimum, constructs the least-favourable schedule from the active block eigenvector, and derives a finite-sample Chebyshev interval from the design-computable radius certificate.
